CLOSED, not viable via CEF's Safe Browsing integration -- confirmed via direct binary/header inspection of the pinned CEF 150.0.14 distribution, going further than the earlier verify-and-close sweep:

(1) Safe Browsing IS compiled in. strings on the CEF framework binary show live, real Chromium Safe Browsing code: the actual v4/v5 hash-lookup endpoints (safebrowsing.googleapis.com/v4, /v5/hashes:search), clientreport/realtime + enterprise reporting endpoints, and genuine preference names (safebrowsing.enabled, safebrowsing.enhanced) -- this is not stripped-out or stubbed code.

(2) It is gated by a Google API key at runtime (google_apis::GetAPIKey(), confirmed via the GOOGLE_API_KEY / GOOGLE_DEFAULT_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_DEFAULT_CLIENT_SECRET env-var strings and the IDS_MISSING_GOOGLE_API_KEYS resource string Chromium itself shows when missing). This is a real, runtime-settable env var (no rebuild needed) -- but Google restricts issuance of a working Safe Browsing key to third-party/non-Chrome-branded embedders, so Brady obtaining one is not guaranteed and is outside this codebase's control.

(3) NEW finding this session, the actual blocker: CEF's entire public embedder API (cef_request_handler.h and everbetter) has ZERO Safe-Browsing-specific hook of any kind -- no interstitial callback, no blocked-navigation handler, nothing named *SafeBrowsing*/*Malware*/*Phishing*/*Interstitial* anywhere in CEF's public headers. Contrast with OnCertificateError, a real documented hook CEF DOES provide for the analogous TLS-cert-error case. So even with a valid API key, there is no confirmed way for this (or any) CEF embedder to intercept a flagged navigation and show a warning -- Chromium's real SafeBrowsingBlockingPage interstitial lives in the //chrome UI layer, which Alloy-style CEF (this project's only supported window style) deliberately doesn't wire up. Wiring the key alone would very likely produce zero user-visible behavior change.

Given both a hard-to-clear external gate (the API key) AND a confirmed missing embedder hook even past that gate, this is a close-with-finding rather than a wire-it -- see browser-12m.6 for the proposed alternative (local malware/phishing domain list via the already-built BlockListCore machinery).

Investigated SharedWithYou's real API surface and requirements. The read path is genuinely there: SWHighlightCenter (macOS 13+) with a delegate-driven .highlights property ([SWHighlight], each wrapping a URL + sender attribution via SWAttributionView) -- a real, documented, non-Safari-specific API per Apple's own docs and WWDC22 session.

The blocker is entitlements, not the API itself: using the framework requires the com.apple.developer.shared-with-you entitlement, and multiple independent developer reports (Apple dev forums, threads 707873/713677/717018, spanning 2022 through recent) describe Xcode/provisioning explicitly REJECTING this entitlement for Developer ID (non-Mac-App-Store) provisioning profiles -- the exact error quoted: "The Shared with You capability is not available for Mac Catalyst Developer ID provisioning profiles. Disable this feature and try again." One report confirms this for a plain AppKit (non-Catalyst) Developer ID app specifically, not just Catalyst. This mirrors Sign in with Apple's own MAS-only restriction. No official Apple statement found either way, and no counter-reports of it working outside the Mac App Store were found either -- but per this app's own docs/plans ("Distribution: Developer ID + notarization only... No Mac App Store"), this is a hard, structural mismatch: even if Apple granted the entitlement case-by-case, this app's whole distribution model is the thing the entitlement appears to be gated against.

Also confirmed: needs the sender to be a Contact, the per-app+per-conversation Messages 'Shared with You' toggle on, and links pinned if self-sent -- real content prerequisites independent of the entitlement question.

Recommend closed, not pursued, unless Brady wants to personally test whether a Developer ID provisioning profile can request this entitlement today (reports may be stale) -- not done here since it needs a real Apple Developer Portal attempt, not something verifiable by code/research alone.

Implemented: scripts/build.sh acquires a mkdir-based lock (build/.build-lock) before touching the shared build/ directory, released via trap on EXIT; a concurrent invocation prints 'waiting for another build to finish' and polls every 2s rather than racing into the database-locked error; a killed/crashed holder's stale lock is detected via kill -0 on its recorded PID and reclaimed. Verified by actually reproducing the race: two concurrent ./scripts/build.sh Debug runs, second one waited and proceeded only after the first released the lock, neither log shows the database-locked error, lock dir confirmed removed after both finished. scripts/release.sh's isolated build-release/ untouched. See commit 4ff868f, docs/ai-tasks/build-lock-notes.md.

Implemented: BRWGetOrCreateProfileContext (BRWEngineInternal.h/BRWEngine.mm) now keys CefRequestContext/cache_path by profile id, not name. Discovered the real blast radius was much wider than just BRWEngine.mm -- almost every per-profile store (browser.db, blocking.json, threat_warning.json, startpage.json, permissions.json, password-never-list.json, addresses, Favicons) shared that same name-keyed directory, so all were switched to id-keyed too (via a new CommandLineArgs.profileDirectory(profileId:) / BrowserCore ProfilesRootResolver.profileDirectory(profilesRoot:profileId:), tested). profileId threaded from BrowserWindowController through Tab/BrowserEngine protocol/CEFEngineAdapter/BRWBrowser to the bridge; WebKitEngineAdapter's own owner picked up the matching protocol-conformance change themselves (commit 6ae00b9). ProfileManager gained a one-time startup migration (migrateNameKeyedDirectoriesIfNeeded) that atomically renames each profile's old name-keyed directory to id-keyed, skipping (not guessing at) any profile where both already exist. updateProfile/deleteProfiles simplified -- renaming a profile no longer moves any directory at all. Verified: 2 new BrowserCore tests (83 total passing), full Debug build green, and three real scratch --profiles-root launches: fresh-profile creation confirmed id-keyed from scratch; migration confirmed via a pre-seeded name-keyed directory with real marker content, preserved byte-for-byte after being renamed to the id-keyed path; the ambiguous both-exist case confirmed left completely untouched with the expected log line. See commit 3fe15a1, docs/ai-tasks/profile-id-cache-directory-notes.md. Still user-verifiable: an actual UI-driven profile rename with a window already open.
